# Atlas compute auto-scaling for sharded clusters — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Atlas compute auto-scaling for sharded clusters. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-23 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] For Atlas Core sharded clusters, Atlas applies the same compute tier auto-scaling criteria as for replica sets. When independent shard scaling is active, Atlas evaluates shards separately and changes the tier only for the operational or analytics node class on a shard that meets a scaling criterion. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-autoscaling-compute-core/ · keywords: Atlas compute auto-scaling for sharded clusters · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-sharding/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/atlas-cli-independent-shard-scaling/
- [statement] Declarative infrastructure controllers can conflict with Atlas auto-scaling. A Crossplane issue reports that reconciliation reset Atlas-scaled cluster tiers to the declared specification. HashiCorp documents `ignore_changes` for attributes managed by an external process, and MongoDB's Terraform provider guide recommends `use_effective_fields` or lifecycle ignore rules for Atlas-managed size changes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://github.com/crossplane-contrib/provider-mongodbatlas/issues/24 · keywords: Atlas compute auto-scaling for sharded clusters · also: https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/meta-arguments/lifecycle, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/master/docs/guides/advanced-cluster-new-sharding-schema.md, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/master/docs/resources/advanced_cluster.md
- [statement] MongoDB's Terraform provider guide says its new sharding configuration enables per-shard instance-size auto-scaling when each shard has a unique `replication_specs` element; this schema removes `num_shards` in provider v2.0.0. Provider PR #2836 reports that a manually tested legacy `num_shards` configuration returned `autoScalingMode: CLUSTER`, while the separate-shard configuration returned `SHARD`. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/master/docs/guides/advanced-cluster-new-sharding-schema.md · keywords: Atlas compute auto-scaling for sharded clusters · also: https://github.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/pull/2836, https://registry.terraform.io/providers/mongodb/mongodbatlas/latest/docs/resources/advanced_cluster, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-sharding/
- [statement] MongoDB's Terraform provider documents `use_effective_fields = true` for dedicated clusters (M10+) as a way to preserve configured specs while exposing Atlas-managed effective values through the data source, avoiding `lifecycle.ignore_changes` when auto-scaling stays enabled. The provider says this setting currently has no effect when a cluster has more than one `replication_specs` entry and recommends not enabling it for multi-shard clusters. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/master/docs/resources/advanced_cluster.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Atlas UI can enable compute auto-scaling so shards scale independently, but it cannot manually set each shard's tier. Per-shard tier changes use the Atlas Administration API, Atlas CLI, or Terraform; after independently scaling shards through those interfaces, the Atlas Cluster Builder UI cannot manage that cluster. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-sharding/ · keywords: Atlas compute auto-scaling for sharded clusters · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/atlas-cli-independent-shard-scaling/, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/master/docs/resources/advanced_cluster.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Atlas documents cluster-wide and independent shard scaling as separate modes. It says sharded clusters created before Dec 9, 2024 default to cluster-wide scaling. The current Atlas CLI guide says omitting `--autoScalingMode` defaults to `clusterWideScaling`; it describes independent mode through a `replicationSpecs` object that represents an individual shard. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-sharding/ · keywords: Atlas compute auto-scaling for sharded clusters · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/atlas-cli-independent-shard-scaling.md
- [statement] The MongoDB Terraform provider guide ties independent compute auto-scaling to the new sharding schema: each shard needs a unique `replication_specs` element, while the legacy `num_shards` grouping remains cluster-wide. A provider change compared the old schema's `autoScalingMode: CLUSTER` with the new schema's `autoScalingMode: SHARD`. (high confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/master/docs/guides/advanced-cluster-new-sharding-schema.md · keywords: Atlas compute auto-scaling for sharded clusters · also: https://github.com/mongodb/terraform-provider-mongodbatlas/pull/2836, https://registry.terraform.io/providers/mongodb/mongodbatlas/latest/docs/resources/advanced_cluster
- [statement] Atlas CLI exposes `clusterWideScaling` and `independentShardScaling` through `--autoScalingMode`; its documentation says omitting the option defaults to `clusterWideScaling`. Atlas's sharding page says clusters created before Dec 9, 2024 use cluster-wide scaling by default. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/atlas-cli-independent-shard-scaling/ · keywords: Atlas compute auto-scaling for sharded clusters · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-sharding/
- [statement] Infrastructure-as-code reconciliation can conflict with Atlas auto-scaling: HashiCorp says Terraform normally plans remote settings back to configuration unless attributes are ignored, and a Crossplane provider user reported Atlas-scaled tier and storage values being reverted during reconciliation. Crossplane maintainers later suggested `spec.initProvider` and closed the issue as completed, but the issue does not identify a released provider version containing the change. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/meta-arguments/lifecycle · keywords: Atlas compute auto-scaling for sharded clusters · also: https://github.com/crossplane-contrib/provider-mongodbatlas/issues/24
